recentItems.title: Russian asset seizure law: Legislation gives govt powers to confiscate property
recentItems.description:
Russia’s sweeping new asset seizure law comes into effect on Tuesday. It gives the government powers to confiscate bank funds and physical property of Russian citizens living abroad. The legislation targets dissidents, journalists, and activists and expands the Kremlin's crackdown on critics of the Ukraine war.

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova reports from Moscow.

recentItems.title: Lesotho's male midwives challenge tradition amid high maternal death rate
recentItems.description:
In Lesotho, a growing number of men are challenging traditional gender roles by becoming midwives as the country struggles with a high rate of maternal deaths. Around 300 male midwives now work in the southern African kingdom, helping provide maternity care in communities where access to health facilities can be limited. The World Health Organization says about 478 women died for every 100,000 live births in Lesotho last year, more than double the global average. While some women still prefer female health workers, others say the quality of care matters more than the gender of the midwife. Supporters believe male midwives can help expand maternity care and bring greater awareness to maternal health. 

Al Jazeera's Cara Legg reports.

recentItems.title: Ghost towns reveal devastation along Sudan's recaptured Exports Road
recentItems.description:
Sudan's army is working to consolidate control of the strategic al-Sadirat, or Exports Road, linking Khartoum with el-Obeid and the wider Kordofan and Darfur regions. 
The route was controlled by the Rapid Support Forces for much of Sudan's three-year conflict before the army recaptured it last month, along with several towns and cities. Burnt vehicles, abandoned buildings and deserted communities along the highway reveal the scale of the fighting. 
Jabrat al-Sheikh, one of the largest towns along the route, has become a ghost town after fierce battles drove civilians away. 
The army is continuing operations to regain territory, while the RSF continues drone attacks on army-controlled areas in Kordofan. Hundreds of thousands of displaced people are still waiting to find out when they can safely return home.

Al Jazeera's Hiba Morgan reports from Jabrat al-Sheikh in North Kordofan.

recentItems.title: Two dead and about 15 people missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon
recentItems.description:
Flash flooding in a remote area of Arizona's Grand Canyon has left 15 people missing, with two bodies recovered. A storm sent a torrent through Bright Angel Canyon and into the Colorado River, sweeping away a cabin, inundating campsites and destroying footbridges and trails. Hikers described hearing a rumbling "like a train" as the flood approached without warning. Helicopters were used to evacuate people as emergency teams continued searching for those missing or trapped. Authorities warned that more storms could bring further flooding. 

Al Jazeera's Caley Callahan reports.
